Y-Character Sheet Lora [works best in 3:2 aspect ratio]
If you want specific clothing, upload a second image of the outfit and add a prompt. Describe the anatomy.

Prompt: Redraw the single character illustration as a character reference sheet showing front and back views, plus close-ups of the head from multiple angles. Place a large head portrait in the center, a headless full-body front view on the left, and a full-body back view on the right. Beneath the large portrait, add two smaller side-view head portraits. Preserve the character’s original clothing and details. Use a white background.

Enhance Lora [Elusarca's Qwen 2.1 Detail Enhancer]
Prompt: Enhance this image to high resolution with rich fine details. Sharpen textures and surfaces, add natural microdetails, and improve clarity and definition across the image while preserving the original composition, lighting, atmosphere, and visual style. The input may be an illustration or a real photograph; preserve the original style.

EDIT PROMPT IDEAS:

Y-change the head of the subject in <image1> to the new head of the subject in <image2>. keep the pose of <image1> but the new face, head and hair of <image2>.

Y-upscale it by just changing the latent size and leaving prompt blank.
Or try: Restore <image1> to a high-resolution, clear, in-focus photography with restored detail. Repair any defects, damage or spots. Remove any JPEG artifacts or compression artifacts. Preserve their identity. Their skin is smooth and natural. [gets rid of watermarks as well without asking!]

Y-Isolate the main subject from <image 1>, remove the background, and output as an RGBA image with a transparent background and alpha channel. [works great!]

Y-replace the texture of wall on <image 1> with the green texture of <image 2>
Example: replace the black and green dot texture of the wall on <image 1> with the wallpaper texture of <image 2>. the black and green dot texture on her dress jacket in <image1> should remain.

Y-change the color of the dress in <image1> to hex color 828A8F and change the boot color in <image1> to hex color 9E1B32.

Y-change the wallpaper in <image1> to clear glass windows showing the skyline of a large city in the background. It's nighttime outside and the stars and moon are shining bright.  There are fireworks in the sky off in the distance.

Y-change the camera location to the ceiling directly above the subject in <image1> looking down at her lap and feet. She is now leaning back in the green chair, looking up.

Y-change the camera location to the floor, close to her orange shoe in <image1> as if a small ant was holding the camera. The lens of the camera is looking up at the woman from that lower angle.

Y-replace the woman in <image1> with the woman from <image2>. keep the same background of <image1>. keep the woman and clothes from <image2>

Y-replace the pink tennis balls in <image1> with the round grenades in <image2>. Keep the placement and consistency of the ball locations in <image1> for the new grenade locations from <image2>.
 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST THESE MORE:
-replace the word "Family" in <image1> with "Bacon". NO change to the background wall or the rest of the image.  [worked ok, not perfect]

-replace the lighting and background on <image 1> with the lighting and background
of <image 2> 4 to 7. transfer the style of <image 1> with the style of <image 2> + more conditionals

-right side view low-angle shot [medium shot] of <image 1>

-<image 1> at night backlight [didn't do great for my tests]

-Show the Family logo from <image2> as if it was stitched into the fabric of the dress on the woman in <image1>.  Change the text to hex color 9E1B32. The text of the logo should resemble thread woven into the gray dress. It should look as if it was created and purchased from the store with that logo added. the gray strings on the dress should go over the text to help create the illusion of reality. 

-change the pose of the woman in <image 1> with the pose of the woman in <image 2>. keep the woman's face, hair and clothing the same from <image 1>.

9/22 new to test:
-Take the style of <image 2> and apply it to <image 1>

-【Character】Use the input reference image as the basis for character design, depict the same person—maintaining consistent face, hairstyle, clothing, and body proportions; only change the pose, expression, actions and camera angle. The reference image should only define the appearance; do not copy the posture. Naturally integrate the character into their respective realistic scenes, ensuring correct perspective proportions and appropriate lighting.

Pose: The head faces forward. The eyes look toward the observer. Overall observable state: casual standing posture with hands in pockets. she is screaming and smiling

Change camera view to the right low angle

-

nodes.title: Note: Usage
widgets_values:
## Size
Qwen Image 2.1 has native 2K (2048*2048) support for direct output.

- resolution is a total pixel budget (not width or height). Aspect ratio is preserved.
- Official default is 1024. The model supports up to 2048.
- This template starts at 0: no resize beyond a multiple of 32.
- Output follows image_1. Extra refs can differ in size or aspect.
- custom_size off: canvas comes from the encode latent (image_1).
- custom_size on: use ResolutionSelector width/height. Keep it close to the resized image_1 size, or the edit can shift.

## Reference images
- Up to 10 reference images (image_1 to image_10).
- Mention them in the prompt as `<image1>`, `<image2>`, ...
- image_1 is the edit target. The rest are references.

## Custom settings
If you need custom settings, enter or unpack the subgraph to edit it. See the [Subgraph](https://docs.comfy.org/interface/features/subgraph) guide.

## Parameters
- prompt: edit instruction. Use `<image1>` ... `<image10>`.
- negative_prompt: unused while cfg is 1.
- cfg: keep 1 for the Qwen Image 2.1 official path. Raise it only if you use a negative prompt.
- steps: Qwen Image 2.1 official pipeline uses about 40-50 with euler. This template starts at 25. More advanced samplers need fewer steps.
